question: A student connects a voltmeter across the terminals of a glowing bulb. What does the voltmeter measure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential difference across the bulb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **voltmeter** is an instrument specifically designed to measure the **potential difference (voltage)** between two points in an electrical circuit.
 
• When connected across the terminals of a glowing bulb, the voltmeter measures the **voltage drop** across the bulb. This drop indicates the amount of electrical energy being consumed by the bulb per unit charge.
 
• The voltmeter operates by having a high internal resistance, which ensures that it does not significantly affect the circuit or draw current during measurement. ***Hence, the voltmeter measures the potential difference across the bulb.***
 
• The voltmeter does not measure the **current through the bulb**, as current measurement requires an ammeter connected in series with the circuit. *Hence, option 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The voltmeter does not directly measure the **heat produced by the bulb**, as heat is a secondary effect of electrical power dissipation. Power can be calculated using the potential difference and current. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The voltmeter cannot measure the **resistance of the bulb**. • **Measurement Devices:**

 
 
• **Ammeter:** Used to measure current, connected in series in the circuit.
 
• **Voltmeter:** Used to measure voltage, connected in parallel.
 
• **Multimeter:** A versatile device that measures voltage, current, and resistance.
 
• **Wattmeter:** Used to measure electrical power.
 
 
 
• **Power and Energy:**
 
 
• Power indicates the rate at which energy is consumed by the bulb.
 
• Energy consumption is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh" id="MathJax-Element-48-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">kWhkWh" id="MathJax-Element-91-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">kWh kWh kWh \text{kWh} ), commonly used in electricity bills.

• **Applications in Daily Life:**
 
 
• Voltage measurement is essential in household appliances to ensure safety and functionality.
 
• Understanding resistance and power helps in choosing energy-efficient devices.
 
• Electrical measurements are vital in industries, laboratories, and renewable energy systems.
